newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil slightly higher on quiet European market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil slightly higher on quiet European market.

text.p: Palm oil prices were showing small gains at midday on Wednesday on the European vegetable oil market in quiet trading.

Higher Chicago futures and news of India's offtake supported prices. But concern in the Far East over Pakistan's future palm oil imports following Tuesday's devaluation of its currrency restricted the upside.
Pakistan's imports of palm oil from Malaysia are seen falling following the devaluation of the rupee by 3.79 percent against the U.S. dollar.

"They will have to pay more for the same oil, but it could take some time before the full impact is known because Pakistan has good stocks and their own edible oil crop will start to come in soon," said a trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe was offered $2.50 to $5 up at midday after Sep traded at $550 and $552.50 in early trading while $545 was paid for Nov/Dec and Jan/Mar at the opening.
Refined palm oil prices were $2.50 higher after Oct RBD palm oil fetched $527.50 and Oct olein $565 and $562.50 with $550 paid for Nov/Dec fob Malaysian ports.
Lauric oils have so far been quiet with coconut oil sellers $5 up and palmkernel oil $20 to $15 above Tuesday's close.
Softs oils were around 1.50 guilders up, with most players awaiting the latest twist in the Chicago weather market saga when the USDA's crop report is released.
